changes.before: At the Cross her station keeping, Stood the mournful Mother weeping, Close to Jesus to the last.
changes.after:
Weeping sore, the Mother stood
Near the Cross, the fatal wood,
Where her Son hung dying.

changes.before: Through her heart, His sorrow sharing, All His bitter anguish bearing Now at length the sword had passed.
changes.after:
Through her soul, in anguish crying,
Sunk in sorrow, spent with sighing,
A sword had pierced her through.

changes.before: Oh, how sad and sore distressed Was that Mother highly blessed Of the sole begotten One!
changes.after:
Oh, how sad, how heavy laden,
Was that meek and blessed Maiden,
Mother of God’s only Son!

changes.before: Christ above in torment hangs, She beneath beholds the pangs Of her dying, glorious Son.
changes.after:
Grieving, bowed beneath her woes,
The loving Mother watched the throes
Of her own glorious Son.

changes.before: Is there one who would not weep, ’Whelmed in miseries so deep, Christ’s dear Mother to behold?
changes.after:
Who could look and fail to weep,
Seeing grief so sore and deep
In the Mother of our Lord?

changes.before: Who would not be saddened on contemplating Christ’s Mother suffering with her Son?
changes.after:
Who could look unmoved
On the Mother of our Lord,
Grieving with her Son?

changes.before: For the sins of His own nation, She saw Jesus’ tribulation, Him with bloody scourges rent.
changes.after:
For the sins of His own people,
She saw Jesus in His torment,
Given over to the scourge.

changes.before: Her sweet Son she saw, her own, Dying desolate, alone, Till His spirit forth He sent.
changes.after:
She beheld her gentle Son,
Dying, desolate, alone,
When He yielded up His spirit.

changes.before: O sweet Mother! fount of love, Let me sorrow’s power prove, Mourning with you in accord.
changes.after:
Come, dear Mother, love’s sweet spring,
Let me feel the force of sorrow,
Let me mourn with you.

changes.before: Make my heart with fire to burn, Loving Christ my God in turn, So that I may please my Lord.
changes.after:
Let my heart be wrapped in fire
With the love of Christ my God,
So that I may please Him.

changes.before: Holy Mother, pierce me through, In my heart each wound renew Of my Savior crucified.
changes.after:
Holy Mother, hear my prayer.
Deeply print upon my heart
All the wounds the Crucified bore.

changes.before: Let me share with you His pain, Who for all our sins was slain, Who for me in torments died.
changes.after:
Share with me the pains He bore,
For your wounded Son was willing
To endure them all for me.

changes.before: Mix’d with yours let my tears be, Mourning Him Who mourned for me, All the days that I may live.
changes.after:
Let our tears in one stream flow
As I grieve with Christ crucified,
All the days that I shall live.

changes.before: By the Cross with you to stay, There with you to weep and pray, Is all I ask of you to give.
changes.after:
By the Cross to take my station
And to share your lamentation
Is my most earnest prayer.

changes.before: Virgin of all virgins blest! Listen to my fond request: Let me share that grief of yours.
changes.after:
Virgin, brightest of all virgins,
Do not turn from me in bitterness.
Let me share your grief.

changes.before: Let me bear the death of Christ, Sharer of His sacrifice, And His holy wounds recall.
changes.after:
Let me bear the very death He bore,
Share with Him in all His Passion,
And remember all His wounds.

changes.before: Wounded with His every wound, Steep my soul till it has swooned In His very Blood away.
changes.after:
Let His wounds be wounds to me.
Let me drink my fill of the Cross
And of the Blood of your dear Son.

changes.before: Be to me, O Virgin, nigh, Lest in flames I burn and die, In His awful judgment day.
changes.after:
Lest I burn amid the flames,
Virgin, guard this soul of mine
When the day of judgment comes.

changes.before: Christ, when You shall call me hence, Through Your Mother, my defense, Bring me to the victor’s prize.
changes.after:
Christ, when these my days are done,
Let Your Mother lead me on
To the palm of victory.

changes.before: When my body comes to die, Grant, O Christ, my soul on high The glory of Paradise. Amen. Alleluia.
changes.after:
When this frail flesh has died,
Grant that my soul may receive
The glory of Paradise. Amen. Alleluia.
